title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Claim Filing and Appeal Windows
content:
For the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, each payer tier fixes how long Larkfield has to file an original claim, to cure an unprocessable denial with a corrected claim, and how long a first-level and a second-level appeal stay open. All windows are in calendar days.

| Tier | Timely filing (from the date of service, the ship date) | Corrected claim after a CO-16 denial (from the denial's posting date) | First-level appeal (from the denial's posting date) | Second-level appeal (from the first-level decision's posting date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CGM Self-Pay Program | 0 (no payer claim is filed) | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (no payer appeal exists) | 0 (none) |
| CGM Commercial HMO Program | 90 | 90 | 180 | 120 |
| CGM Commercial PPO Program | 180 | 180 | 180 | 120 |
| CGM Medicare Advantage Program | 180 | 180 | 65 | 0 |
| CGM Original Medicare Program | 365 | 365 | 120 | 180 |
| CGM Medicaid Program | 365 | 365 | 60 | 120 |

## Notes to the table

1. **First-level appeal** means the commercial internal appeal, the Medicare Advantage reconsideration, the Medicare redetermination or the Medicaid plan appeal, according to the tier.
2. **Second-level appeal** means the commercial external review, the Medicare QIC reconsideration or the Medicaid state fair hearing, according to the tier. A figure of 0 means there is no customer-filed second level: on the CGM Self-Pay Program there is none at all, and on the CGM Medicare Advantage Program the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity automatically.
3. A figure of 0 in the timely-filing column means no payer claim is filed on that tier; a 0 in the corrected-claim column means the window does not apply.

## Comparing tiers

- The shortest timely-filing window belongs to the CGM Commercial HMO Program (90 days); the CGM Original Medicare Program and the CGM Medicaid Program allow 365 days.
- The CGM Medicare Advantage Program has a first-level window of 65 days and no customer-filed second level.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

On a hypothetical tier with a 60-day first-level window, a denial posted on 1 March of a hypothetical non-leap year stays appealable through 30 April, the sixtieth calendar day after the posting date; 1 May is outside the window.
